requests.title: Requests
requests.subtitle: {{shown}} of {{logged}} requests · {{range}}
requests.note: A 429 row is not an error the client saw — it is a failover step, and the row after it serves the same turn from the next target in the chain. Failed upstream attempts are not recorded yet, though: the pipeline throws before the usage capture runs, so a count of 0 here does not mean no failover happened. Subscription rows are priced at list price — the plan is already paid for.

chain.title: Routing
chain.explainerRouted: Routed applies scenarios, rules and quota-aware failover. Passthrough sends the caller's <mono>provider,model</mono> straight upstream.
chain.explainerPassthrough: Passthrough sends the caller's <mono>provider,model</mono> straight upstream. Routed applies scenarios, rules and quota-aware failover.
chain.noTargetsLeft: Every target is already in this chain.
chain.emptyLane: This lane has no targets yet.
chain.note: Order is preference, top first: the router walks the chain and sends the request to the first target it can use, so <mono>Share</mono> is each target's slice of this lane's scheduler weight — not the fraction of traffic it will see. A target is skipped when it is disabled, exhausted, or its share is <mono>0%</mono>. The weights are published by the routing scheduler every tick — edit the chain, not the numbers.
chain.unconfiguredProfile: Profile <mono>{{profile}}</mono> has no entries, so requests on <mono>{{path}}</mono> fall through to the scenario router. Add a target to take the decision here instead.
chain.noLaneRules: No rules apply to this lane.
chain.quotaSkipHint: skip accounts the quota collector reports as spent
chain.reachableHint: what a caller may put in <mono>body.model</mono>
chain.passthroughNote: Switch this surface to <mono>Routed</mono> to give {{client}} the same quota-aware failover Claude Code gets. Callers keep sending their own model string — it becomes the <mono>requestedModel</mono> that rules match on, rather than the final target.
chain.schedulerIdle: The <mono>Rules</mono> selector is active, so this chain is not evaluated and every target below reads <mono>unknown</mono>. Switch the selector above to <mono>Chain</mono> to let it decide; the states fill in on the scheduler’s next tick.
chain.schedulerNoChain: The routing scheduler is running but has no preference chain to score, so every target below reads <mono>unknown</mono>. Add entries to this surface’s routing profile to see live states.
chain.schedulerNotTicked: The routing scheduler has not published a snapshot yet, so every target below reads <mono>unknown</mono>. States fill in on its first tick — by default within five minutes of the server starting.

map.title: Routing map
map.canvasTitle: Surfaces, scenarios and targets, and the edges between them
map.note: Dashed edges bypass the router entirely — that surface is in passthrough and jumps straight to whatever target the caller named.

rules.selectOne: Select a rule to edit it.
rules.explainer: Evaluated top to bottom against the request; the first match replaces the target outright and brings its own failover chain. With the <mono>Chain</mono> selector active a scenario whose chain has entries decides instead, and the rule’s target is dropped — the two never combine.

server.subtitle: Rialto v{{version}} · config envelope on disk
server.headerNote: Boot-time values. A change takes effect when the server restarts — `docker compose restart`, or restart the process.
server.numbersRequired: Port and request timeout must be whole numbers.
server.hostHint: Bind address. Put Cloudflare Access in front before exposing beyond loopback.
server.bootstrapTokenHint: Gates /api/* only — the admin recovery path. Clients call /v1/* with an issued access token.
server.requestTimeoutHint: Milliseconds. Applies to every upstream call.
server.proxyUrlHint: Routes upstream traffic through an HTTPS proxy.
server.nonInteractiveHint: Skip prompts that expect a TTY.
server.homeDirectoryHint: Config envelope, plugins, tokenizer cache. Not surfaced by the API.

logging.subtitle: level {{level}} · {{captured}} captured
logging.headerNote: pino, to the logs directory under the config home
logging.writeToFileHint: Off keeps logging to stdout only.
logging.levelHint: fatal · error · warn · info · debug · trace
logging.rotateAtHint: Megabytes. A new file is started past this size.
logging.rotateSizeInvalid: Rotate size must be a whole number of megabytes above zero.
logging.recordRequestsHint: One RequestLog row per upstream call — tokens, cost, latency, routing decision.
logging.recordMessagesHint: Chat turns for the session view. Never includes the system prompt or tool definitions.
logging.redactToolArgsHint: Store tool_use blocks with arguments stripped.
logging.privacyBody: User and assistant turns are written to Postgres in the clear so the session view can replay them. Turn Record messages off if this database is shared, or prune the Message store below. Anything not recorded is gone for good: Usage and cost keep a permanent gap for the period capture was off, and redaction is applied before the turn is stored.
logging.retentionNote: The cutoff above is the argument to the button beside it, not a stored policy — nothing prunes on a schedule. Sizes include indexes and TOAST.
logging.pruneConfirm: Delete {{store}} {{unit}} older than {{days}} days? This cannot be undone.
logging.pruneWarnRequestLog: Usage and cost totals are computed from these rows, so historical spend figures will drop.
logging.pruneWarnMessage: The session view replays these turns; pruned conversations can no longer be read back.

advanced.subtitle: config document · health
advanced.statusHint: Degraded means the server answered but a dependency check failed. Unreachable means it did not answer at all.
advanced.reportedVersionHint: The version the running process believes it is.
advanced.dependencyChecksHint: One entry per dependency the probe touches.
advanced.archiveAllHint: Clears the Activity session list. RequestLog rows stay, so usage history and cost totals are preserved, and a session reappears the moment it sees new traffic.
advanced.archiveConfirm: Archive every active session? They drop out of Activity; usage and cost totals are kept.
advanced.resetWhat: Reset routing · re-seed catalog · purge captured data
advanced.resetNeeds: All three are destructive operations with no route behind them. They need server-side handlers that can do the work inside one transaction; a client-side loop over the existing per-row endpoints would leave a half-reset install behind on any failure.
advanced.readFailed: Could not read the config document: {{message}}
advanced.cannotFormat: Cannot format: the document does not parse.
advanced.cannotSave: Cannot save: the document does not parse.
advanced.backupsKept: no backups — this is the only copy
advanced.configNote: <mono>$VAR</mono> is interpolated at boot, so a key can live in the environment rather than this file. Saving overwrites the file in place and there is no backup to roll back to — take your own copy first if the change is large. The file on disk is JSON5 and keeps its comments; this view is the composed document the API returns, so saving from here rewrites it as plain JSON. Boot scalars need a restart — the screens above apply live.

access.subtitleConfigured: Cloudflare Access on /api · scoped tokens on /v1
access.subtitleUnconfigured: Bootstrap token only on /api · scoped tokens on /v1
access.signedInAsHint: The caller Rialto verified for this request.
access.exposureNotice: Cloudflare Access is not configured — the bootstrap token alone gates /api/*, so anyone holding it has full administrative control. Fill in the team domain and AUD below to put an identity check in front of it.
access.envelopeReadFailed: Could not read the config envelope: {{message}}
access.identityReadFailed: Could not read the caller identity: {{message}}
access.savedOff: Access turned off. /api/* now accepts the bootstrap token only.
access.savedOn: Access settings saved. They apply to the next request — reload to confirm you are still let in.
access.teamDomainHint: Looks like <team>.cloudflareaccess.com. Required together with the AUD tag — one alone enables nothing.
access.applicationAudHint: The Application Audience tag from the Access app. Without it a token minted for any other app on your team would be accepted.
access.verifyHint: Nothing is saved by this. It reports whether these values would work.
access.checkStale: Values changed since this check — run it again.
access.policyCoverageHint: Which Access apps sit on this hostname.
access.policyListingUnavailable: Listing the Access apps needs a Cloudflare API token and a Zero Trust proxy — check them in the dashboard.
access.bypassNote: /v1 must be a Bypass policy. Claude Code, Codex and Gemini CLI cannot complete an interactive Access login, so putting Access in front of that path locks every client out — the access tokens below are its gate instead.
access.apikeyHint: Stored in the on-disk envelope and mirrored onto process.env. Accepted on /api/* only — the recovery path when Access or the database is down. The proxy refuses it.
access.clipboardRefused: Clipboard write was refused by the browser.
access.guardAccessBody: Guards this UI and <mono>/api/*</mono>. The browser logs in at the edge and Rialto verifies the signed assertion against your team's JWKS before the request reaches a handler.
access.guardTokenBody: Guards <mono>/v1/*</mono>. CLI clients cannot complete an interactive Access login, so that path is a Bypass app and these per-client tokens are its gate.
access.guardProviderBody: Outbound. Rialto presents it to a vendor. Lives on the provider in Providers.
access.tokensNote: Only the SHA-256 digest is stored, so the plaintext is shown once, at issue. These are the only credentials /v1/* accepts. Scoping to an endpoint and a profile gives one client its own routing. Open a row to rotate it — a new secret on the same row, keeping its name, scope and history — or to revoke it.
access.issueNameHint: How this client is identified in the list and in Activity.
access.issueEndpointHint: Pick the endpoints this token may call. Choose several when one client speaks more than one — Codex uses both /v1/responses and /v1/chat/completions. All endpoints leaves it unrestricted.
access.issueProfileHint: Route this client's traffic through a named profile. Unset follows the endpoint's own routing.
access.issueExpiresHint: A bounded token limits the damage if it leaks. Revoke works either way.
access.issueOnceNote: The token is shown once, immediately after issuing, and never again.
access.issuedBody: This is the only time the full token is shown. Rialto stores a SHA-256 digest, so it cannot be recovered — only replaced by issuing another.
access.issuedCopyRefused: Clipboard write was refused — select the token and copy it manually.
access.issuedDismissConfirm: Close without copying? The token cannot be shown again — you would have to reissue.
access.revokeConfirm: Revoke "{{name}}"? Any client using it stops working immediately.
access.deleteConfirm:
Delete "{{name}}" permanently?

It is already revoked, so this changes nothing about access. What it does lose is attribution: past requests in Activity will no longer resolve to this token's name.
access.noTokensTitle: No tokens issued — the proxy is closed
access.noTokensBody: <mono>/v1/*</mono> accepts issued access tokens and nothing else; the bootstrap token is refused there. Until you issue one, no client can route a request — Claude Code, Codex and the OpenAI SDK will all get a 401. That is the intended default: closed until you decide who may call.
access.costNote: The Cost column prices the last 30 days of retained request logs — a rate, not the lifetime total the counter beside it shows. A dash means nothing priced: no traffic in the window, capture off, or a subscription model, which has no per-request price.
access.closedNotice: Remote admin access is closed — no bootstrap token is set and Cloudflare Access is not configured, so only a browser on this machine can reach /api/*. Set a team domain and AUD below to open it to a verified identity.
access.rotateConfirm: Rotate “{{name}}”? The current token stops working immediately, and the replacement is shown once.
access.rotateRefusedRevoked: This token is revoked, so a new secret on it would not work either. Issue a new token instead.
access.rotateRefusedExpired: This token has expired, so a new secret on it would not work either. Issue a new token instead.
access.rotatedBody: The previous value stopped working the moment this one was generated. Copy it now — like every token, it is shown once and stored only as a SHA-256 digest.
access.rotateNote: Rotating keeps this row. The name, endpoint scope, routing profile and every request already attributed to this token stay as they are; only the secret the client presents changes.
access.detailUsageHint: Requests served, spend over the last 30 days, and when this token was last seen.
access.detailLifetimeHint: When this token was created, when it stops working, and when its secret last changed.
access.scopeSaved: Updated “{{name}}”. The change applies to its next request.
access.scopeEditNote: Saves the endpoint and profile of {{name}}, from its next request. The token value itself does not change.
access.tokenSubtitle: Rotate, re-scope or revoke one client’s credential

personas.promptPlaceholder: Write the persona as you would write it in a system prompt.
personas.previewEmpty: This persona is empty — nothing is prepended.

accessRejected.title: Access token not accepted
accessRejected.body: A <mono>Cf-Access-Jwt-Assertion</mono> header arrived but failed verification. Rialto will not serve <mono>/api/*</mono> until it does.
accessRejected.remedy: Set <mono>ACCESS_AUD</mono> to this application's AUD tag from Zero Trust, or reach the origin through the tunnel rather than directly.

oauth.connectedBody: Tokens stored encrypted. You can close this tab — the Providers screen has already updated.
oauth.failedBody: The provider returned an error before Rialto could exchange the code. Nothing was stored.

unreachable.title: Cannot reach the Rialto API
unreachable.body: The UI is loaded but <mono>/api/config</mono> is not answering. The proxy at <mono>/v1/*</mono> may still be serving requests from its cached configuration — check before restarting.

crash.title: This screen failed to render
crash.body: The server may be fine — this is a fault in the page itself. Reloading is worth trying; if it repeats, the message below is what to report.

setup.intro: Rialto sits between your coding clients and the model vendors. Clients speak whichever wire format they already speak — <mono>/v1/messages</mono>, <mono>/v1/chat/completions</mono>, <mono>/v1/responses</mono>, or Gemini's — and Rialto decides which model actually serves each request, failing over when a subscription runs out of quota.
setup.connectBody: Rialto needs at least one place to send requests. A subscription (Claude / Codex / Gemini) reuses a plan you already pay for; an API key bills per token.
setup.clientBody: The proxy answers only to an issued access token — a fresh install can serve nothing until one exists. Issue one, export it with the base URL, then run your client as usual.
setup.nothingCanCall: Nothing can call the proxy yet.
setup.clipboardRefused: Clipboard was refused — select the token above and copy it by hand.
setup.shownOnce: Shown once. Rialto stores only a hash of it, so leaving this page loses the value — issuing a replacement is the only way back.
setup.footerNote: The token in <mono>~/.rialto/config.json</mono> signs you into this UI. Clients use an access token.
setup.databaseBody: Migrations applied and the model catalog seeded. Registered providers: {{n}} — {{authenticated}}.
setup.alreadyHave: Live tokens so far: {{n}}. Issue another, or paste one you saved — the plaintext of an existing token cannot be shown again.
